context: Use explicit normalized alias handling rather than a bare auth/key substring; add behavior tests through sanitize_platform_options and the exported payload so key visibility and non-secret tuning values remain intact.
description: sanitize_platform_options currently redacts password/token/key families but leaves common credential aliases passwd, pwd, and pat verbatim. A driven ResultExporter(anonymize=False) payload contained PASSWD_SECRET, PWD_SECRET, and PAT_SECRET in platform.raw_config. Cover these aliases in both internal and public result boundaries without substring-redacting legitimate tuning keys such as sort_key or partition_key.

preserves.behavior: nested mapping and tuple sanitization behavior
sort_key, partition_key, primary_key, and other tuning values

verifications.command: PYTHONPATH=. uv run --all-extras -- python -c 'from benchbox.core.results.platform_options import sanitize_platform_options; out=sanitize_platform_options({"passwd":"PASSWD_SECRET","pwd":"PWD_SECRET","pat":"PAT_SECRET","sort_key":"o_orderkey","threads":4}); assert all(out[k]=="<redacted>" for k in ("passwd","pwd","pat")) and out["sort_key"]=="o_orderkey" and out["threads"]==4'
verifications.description: common credential aliases are redacted by the actual sanitizer
verifications.expected: exits 1 on an unfixed tree because credential aliases survive; exits 0 after explicit alias redaction

verifications.description: platform option capture regression suite stays green
verifications.expected: passes before and after as a regression guard
